test_title: RRB NTPC - UG 2025 (CBT 1) Advanced Full Test - 04
subject: general
question: The “One Health” approach in wildlife conservation, as highlighted in the context of mountain gorilla protection in Central Africa, primarily refers to:

options.text: A coordinated disease-control framework that integrates veterinary surveillance with human epidemiology, while treating ecosystem health as an indirect externality.
A conservation strategy that links wildlife tourism revenues to local public health services without formal integration of environmental health governance.
An integrated framework recognising the interdependence of human health, animal health and ecosystem health in policy and practice.
A multi-sectoral zoonoses control model that focuses on preventing animal-to-human transmission through biosecurity protocols and habitat segregation.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3 **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• Conservation of mountain gorillas in Uganda has been linked with public health and community engagement through the One Health approach, improving outcomes for wildlife and local livelihoods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• One Health explicitly integrates human, animal and ecosystem health into a single policy and practice framework. **Hence, Option C is correct. **
 
• Treating ecosystem health as an externality contradicts One Health’s core premise of interdependence.** Hence, Option A is incorrect. **
 
• Linking tourism revenue to public health services does not capture the tri-sectoral integration central to One Health. **Hence, Option B is incorrect. **
 
• Zoonoses control is a subset of One Health; restricting it to biosecurity and habitat segregation narrows the concept improperly. **Hence, Option D is incorrect. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One Health is endorsed by WHO, FAO, UNEP and WOAH.
 
• The approach is applied to zoonoses, AMR, food safety and ecosystem degradation.
 
• Mountain gorillas (Gorilla beringei) are listed in CITES Appendix I.
 
• Community co-management enhances conservation outcomes and compliance.
